Package com.bilt.pos.widget

Interface Surface

All Known Implementing Classes:
WebSurface
public interface Surface
A place on the register where a widget can draw a Rendering.

The surface is the register's side of the widget seam. It owns pixels and input; the widget owns the decision of what to show. The register provides one — a native adapter from a platform module, a WebSurface subclass around its browser control, or its own implementation — and the widget drives it with exactly two verbs.

Threading contract

Both methods are invoked on the owning widget's executor, one call at a time, never concurrently with each other. A surface that draws on a UI thread marshals the call there and returns immediately; it must not block the widget waiting for the frame. Conversely, the callbacks a surface makes into the ActionSink may come from any thread — a UI thread, a JavaScript bridge thread — and the sink marshals back to the widget. A surface should hold no lock while calling the sink.

Replacement and idempotence

show(com.bilt.pos.widget.Rendering, com.bilt.pos.widget.ActionSink) replaces whatever is currently displayed, including a rendering still playing; there is no stacking. clear() removes the current rendering and is idempotent: clearing an empty surface is a no-op, and clearing twice is the same as clearing once. A surface that is cleared must stop reporting interactions for the rendering it was showing.

Capability hints

supportedFormats() and kind() describe the surface to the widget, which folds them into the Capabilities it sends with every decision so the platform only serves what the register can draw. Both have defaults suited to a native adapter that plays everything; a surface that cannot play video, or that draws in some other way, overrides them.

  • Method Details

    • supportedFormats

      default Set<MediaSpec.MediaType> supportedFormats()
      The media formats this surface can draw. The default is every MediaSpec.MediaType; a surface without a video player, say, returns the formats it does handle so the platform never serves it a video.

    • kind

      default SurfaceKind kind()
      How this surface draws, one of the tiers in the com.bilt.pos.widget package documentation. The default is SurfaceKind.NATIVE; WebSurface answers SurfaceKind.WEB, and a hand-off or hosted surface says so, since the kind affects which formats and actions make sense for the platform to serve.

    • show

      void show(Rendering rendering, ActionSink actions)
      Draws rendering, replacing anything currently shown, and reports the shopper's interactions with it to actions. The sink is bound to this rendering: a surface hands back the rendering's own Cta instances and never a token it made up.

    • clear

      void clear()
      Removes the current rendering, if any. Idempotent.
